headline: Dartmouth Health launches $20 million plan to expand care at home
dek: A gift from Dartmouth alumnus Richard Levy will fund home-based primary and palliative care, caregiver training and research aimed at rural patients across northern New England.
body: Dartmouth Health and Dartmouth’s Geisel School of Medicine are launching a new rural-health initiative with a $20 million gift from alumnus Richard “Dick” Levy, a plan that will bring more primary and palliative care into patients’ homes and create a formal support system for family caregivers. The institutions announced Dartmouth Health at Home on Sept. 29. (https://home.dartmouth.edu/news/2026/09/historic-20-million-gift-launch-dartmouth-health-home)

The initiative is built around three connected pieces. A new Family Caregiver Institute will offer practical training, services, resource navigation and access to home-care aides. Dartmouth Health also plans to provide primary and palliative services in patients’ homes, while researchers at The Dartmouth Institute for Health Policy and Clinical Practice study patient outcomes, costs and experiences. The stated goal is to develop a model that can be tested locally and adapted by other health systems.

For New Hampshire, the proposal arrives as families and providers confront the demands of an aging, rural population. New Hampshire Public Radio, republishing reporting by the Concord Monitor, described the initiative as a response to the difficulty of caring for people with progressive illness when medical services, caregivers and transportation are spread across long distances. The report said more than one-quarter of New Hampshire residents are over age 59 and cited a projection of a 503-bed assisted-living shortfall in Merrimack County by 2035. (https://www.nhpr.org/health/2026-09-30/dartmouth-health-athome-primary-care-program-geisel)

Levy’s own experience shaped the gift. After his wife, Susan, was diagnosed with Lewy body dementia, he became her primary caregiver and managed medical needs at home until her death in 2023. He told NHPR that he had to learn tasks such as coordinating care and handling medical needs through trial and error. The new institute is intended to give families more instruction and connections before they are left to assemble that system on their own.

The need extends beyond professional home-health visits. NHPR reported that caregivers may have to administer injections, manage medicines and operate medical equipment, while only 22% of caregivers in a recent study received training. Dartmouth’s announcement said the program will focus on hands-on assistance and coordination rather than treating caregiver support as a passive information service. That distinction matters in rural communities, where a family member may be the person filling gaps between hospital, clinic and home.

Dartmouth Health at Home also builds on an earlier $10 million gift announced in June for the Vickie French Hospital at Home program. That effort is designed to deliver hospital-level services in patients’ homes, including acute care, earlier discharge, post-operative monitoring, palliative care and rehabilitation. Dartmouth Health says the new initiative and the hospital-at-home program are part of a broader shift away from making every patient travel to a traditional facility for care. (https://www.dartmouth-health.org/about/news/article/dartmouth-health-announces-10-million-gift-launch-vickie-french-hospital-home-part-dartmouth)

The rollout is still ahead, not a service already available to every Dartmouth Health patient. NHPR reported that the team hopes to have the different services fully operational by March 2027, with patient enrollment potentially beginning in January. Researchers will be watching whether home-based care improves health outcomes and reduces costs for patients, insurers and the health system. That evaluation will determine how much of Dartmouth’s model can be sustained in New Hampshire and extended to other rural regions.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Dartmouth Health launches $20 million home-care initiative
seoDescription: Dartmouth Health and Geisel will use a $20 million gift to expand home-based care and caregiver support across rural northern New England.
sourceName: New Hampshire Public Radio, reporting by Concord Monitor
